Kāñcīpuram
------------------------------------------
Kāñcīpuram—also spelt as Kañci, Kāñcī, Conjeevaram—is one of the seven very ancient cities and pilgrim centres. It is situated on the bank of Pālār river, at a distance of 75 kms. (46 miles) to the south-west of Chennai (or Madras city) and very near Chengleput (the district head-quarters). काञ्चीपुरम् is a city of temples. It is divided into Śivakāñcī and Viṣṇukāñcī. Temples of Ekāmranātha (also called Ekāmbareśvara), Kailāsanātha and कामाक्षी adorn the former. The latter has the Varadarājasvāmi temple.
The tower of the Ekāmbaranātha temple (of शिव) is majestic and is 56 metres (188 ft.) high. Its high compound encloses an area of 10 hectares (25 acres) and contains the images of 63 Nāyanmārs (Śaiva saints of Tamil Nadu). The temple has been renovated during the recent years.
The next in importance among the temples of Śivakāñcī is the कामाक्षी temple. It is one of the most well-known शक्तिपीठस् (abodes of Divine मोथेर्). A श्रीचक्र in the form of a disc (See ŚRĪCAKRA.) in front of the image receives all the worship. There is also a shrine of Śaṅkarācārya (A.

-820) in the temple complex which is 1.6 hectares (4 acres) in area. The sacred tank in the complex is called Pañcagaṅgā. The annual temple festival takes place in the Tamil month of Māśi (February-March) which includes a silver-car festival also.
The most famous temple of Viṣṇukāñcī is that of वरदराज. It is situated on a small hillock called Hastigiri and is 360 metres by 240 metres (1200 ft. by 800 ft.). The image of वरदराज (an aspect of विष्णु) is quite big in size and is in the standing posture. There are images of the आऌवार्स् and Rāmānuja (A.

-1137) which also receive worship.
Another temple of importance is that of वैकुण्ठ Perumāḷ built in the 8th century A. D. The विमान (tower) of this temple is in three storeys and contains three images in the standing, sitting and recumbent postures.
A rare temple of चित्रगुप्त with his image holding a book of palmyrah leaves is also in काञ्चीपुरम्. It is visited by both the Śaivas and the Vaiṣṇavas.
Kāñcīpuram has been associated with many famous persons. चाणक्य, (300 B. C.) the author of Arthaśāstra is said to have been born here. So also श्यामाशास्त्रि (A.
-1827) a famous musician-saint of South India. बुद्ध (563-483 B. C.), शङ्कर and वेदान्त देशिक (A.

-1369) had visited this place. The पल्लवस् and the Coḷas had ruled here. बुद्धिस्म् and जैनिस्म् had had their heydays at some time here.
The town is famous for Sanskrit learning as also for silk sarees.
See also KĀMĀKṢĪ.
